scene.bubble: Read Sofía's story for story night, learn the adverbs that bring a story alive, then write your own.
scene.intro: The Inspiring Nordic year has a story night, and everyone tells a tale. In this unit you read a short story that Sofía wrote, you learn the adverbs of manner — the words that say HOW something happens — and then you write your own story. Good stories need good adverbs: the fox moves slowly, then suddenly it jumps! We are also reading Matilda, a girl who loves books just like you. Turn the page — it's story time.

activities.title: Reading — a story for story night

data.author: sofia
data.title: The book that opened by itself
data.text:
It was late, and the school library was very quiet. Sofía walked in slowly to return her book. Suddenly, she heard a soft noise near the window.

She looked carefully between the shelves. There, on a small table, an old book was open — but nobody was there! Sofía's heart beat quickly. Was it a ghost, like in a story?

She walked closer and looked at the page. It was Matilda, her favourite book. Then she smiled: the window was open, and the wind was gently turning the pages.

Sofía closed the window quietly and picked up the book. She read the first page again, and finally she understood something. Books are a little like magic — they open new worlds, even on a windy night.

The next day, she told the story to her class, and everyone listened happily. It was the best story of the Inspiring Nordic story night.

data.title: Adverbs of manner
data.intro: Adverbs of manner tell us HOW we do something. We usually make them by adding -ly to an adjective.
rules: Make most adverbs of manner by adding -ly to the adjective: quiet → quietly, happy → happily.
Adverbs of manner usually go after the verb or after the object: She reads quietly.
Some words are irregular: good → well, fast → fast.

data.voice_note: Voz: narrador tranquilo, tono de cuento.
data.script: Listen to the start of Mateo's story for our Inspiring Nordic story night. One cold morning, a small girl called Mia walked slowly to school. Suddenly, she saw a little bird with a hurt wing on the ground. Carefully, she picked it up and put it in her warm hat. All day, the bird slept quietly. Finally, after school, Mia took it home and her family helped it get better. In the spring, the bird flew happily back to the trees.

activities.title: Speaking — tell a one-minute story. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: Prepare a one-minute story to tell your group, like a mini TED talk. Use at least four of these adverbs: suddenly, slowly, carefully, quietly, finally. Model: “One morning I walked slowly to school. Suddenly, I saw…” Your story can be true or invented. Then record your best telling.

homework.prompt: Write a short story (6–8 sentences) for our Inspiring Nordic story night. Use at least four adverbs (for example: slowly, suddenly, carefully, quietly, finally). Give your story a beginning, a middle and an end. Capital letters and full stops!

outcomes.puede: Catch the key points of a short story and write the missing word in each gap (A2 Key Listening).
Tell a short story out loud using adverbs of manner (mini TED talk).
Read a simple story and understand the events and feelings (A2 Key Reading).
Write a short story with a beginning, a middle and an end, using adverbs (A2 Key Writing Part 7).
